historical_references.reference: Ashfaaq ibn Qais was a legendary hero from the pre-Islamic Arabian Peninsula. He was said to have lived during the Jawamid period, around the 6th century AD. Ashfaaq was known for his exceptional physical strength and bravery, and was often invoked in Arabian folklore as a symbol of heroism and defiance against oppression.

Ashfaaq al-Thaqafi was an early Islamic scholar and poet from the city of Kufa, in present-day Iraq. He lived during the Umayyad Caliphate, around the late 7th to early 8th century AD. Ashfaaq is famous for his poetry and his role in the development of Arabic literature during the early Islamic period. He was also a close associate of the famous poet Imru' al-Qais and is considered an important figure in the history of Arabic poetry.
